html:
Spanish Louisiana, or Luisiana, was the huge territory west of the Mississippi River, with New Orleans, that France gave to Spain in 1762. The map shows it in 1783 and 1800, reaching from the Gulf of Mexico to the northern plains.

Spain took it as a buffer to guard Mexico and to keep it out of British hands. Its French settlers rose against the first Spanish governor in 1768, and Alejandro O'Reilly put them down in 1769. Most of the land stayed under the control of Native nations, and the colony's settlers lived along the lower river.

During the American Revolution the governor Bernardo de Gálvez took the British forts of West Florida, from Baton Rouge to Pensacola, between 1779 and 1781. In the secret Treaty of San Ildefonso of 1800 Spain returned Louisiana to France. Napoleon sold it to the United States in the Louisiana Purchase of 1803. For the French colony before 1762, see French Louisiana.
